narrative:
The model predicts an 18% chance that you will fail your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your background. First, having no past class failures actually worked in your favor and pushed the model toward thinking you would pass. Second, your strong desire to pursue higher education also pulled the prediction in a positive direction. However, the single most influential factor was that you did not attend nursery school. This absence of early childhood education had the strongest negative effect, outweighing the other two and tipping the overall prediction toward failure.

Because the model sees early educational foundations as especially important, your lack of nursery experience became the dominant reason for the cautionary decision, even though you are a 15-year-old girl with no previous failures, supportive parents living together, good family relationships, very low alcohol use, and a clear ambition for university.

To improve, focus on building the study habits and foundational skills that nursery and early schooling normally provide. Use the remedial courses to strengthen your basics, keep up your current good intentions around higher education, and consider asking teachers for extra support in areas where you feel less prepared. Small, consistent improvements now can still change the outcome before the final exams.
